title: Cap. VI open: Orthodox position set out — election from mere divine good pleasure
latin: Cap. VI. Orthodoxa sententia exponitur et confirmatur. Accepistis adversariorum argumenta pro illa electione, quam ex antecedaneo voluntatis humanae actu arcessunt. Restat ut nostra jam in medium proferantur, quae electionem sive praedestinationem singularium personarum ad infallibilem consecutionem vitae aeternae, ex mero Dei misericordiae beneplacito dimanare ostendent.
pass_a: Chapter VI. The Orthodox position is set forth and confirmed. You have received the adversaries' arguments for that election which they fetch from an antecedent act of the human will. It remains that ours now be brought into the midst, which will show that the election or predestination of singular persons to the infallible attainment of eternal life flows from the mere good pleasure of the mercy of God.
pass_b: Cap. VI. The orthodox position is set out and confirmed. You have heard the adversaries' arguments for an election they fetch from an antecedent act of the human will. It remains to bring ours forward — showing that election or predestination of singular persons to the infallible attainment of eternal life flows from the mere good pleasure of God's mercy.

lemmas.gloss: mere good pleasure of God's mercy

title: Cap. VI: Remonstrants claim grace-only, but foresight faith still makes dignity the discriminator
latin: Neque tamen me latet Remonstrantes passim obtendere, electionem quam ipsi propugnant inniti sola gratia et misericordia Dei, non ullis meritis aut dignitate hominum. Verum cum totum discrimen electorum et non-electorum revocent ad praevisam fidem et infidelitatem eorundem, manifestum est id discriminis ad dignitatem et indignitatem hominum revocari. Nam fides Petri et perseverantia in fide habet in se moralem quandam dignitatem; sicuti incredulitas Judae et obstinatio in eadem, moralem indignitatem. Quod eo magis elucet, quia haec ipsa fides et perseverantia Petri non illi praeparata ex speciali aliquo Dei beneplacito, aut donata ex speciali aliqua munificentia, supponitur, sed oblata tantum in sufficienti mediorum administratione, sicuti etiam fuit illis qui increduli manserunt, a Petro autem per bonum usum liberi sui arbitrii acquisita et retenta; unde Petri electio est consecuta.
pass_a: Nor yet is it hidden from me that the Remonstrants everywhere put forward that the election which they themselves defend rests on the grace and mercy of God alone, not on any merits or dignity of men. But since they revoke the whole discrimination of the elect and non-elect to the foresight faith and unbelief of the same, it is plain that that discrimination is revoked to the dignity and undignity of men. For the faith of Peter and perseverance in faith has in itself a certain moral dignity; as the unbelief of Judas and obstinacy in the same has a moral undignity. Which shines forth the more, because this very faith and perseverance of Peter is supposed not prepared for him from some special good pleasure of God, or gifted from some special munificence, but only offered in a sufficient administration of means, as it was also to those who remained unbelieving, but acquired and retained by Peter through the good use of his free choice; whence Peter's election followed.
pass_b: I am not unaware that Remonstrants everywhere claim the election they defend rests on God's grace and mercy alone, not on any human merits or dignity. But when they revoke the whole elect/non-elect discrimination to foresight of faith and unbelief, that discrimination is clearly revoked to human dignity and undignity. Peter's faith and perseverance have a certain moral dignity; Judas's unbelief and obstinacy a moral undignity. It shines the more because Peter's faith and perseverance are not supposed prepared by some special divine good pleasure or gifted by special munificence — only offered in a sufficient administration of means, as also to those who remained unbelieving — and acquired and kept by Peter through good use of free choice; whence his election followed.

title: Cap. VI: their questions dissolve by human will; ours ascend to special good pleasure
latin: Ex horum igitur sententia, si quaeratur, Cur hi crediderunt, illi non crediderunt? Cur hi perseveraverunt, illi non perseveraverunt? Cur hi ad vitam aeternam praedestinati fuerunt, illi non fuerunt? hae omnes quaestiones per humani arbitrii velle et nolle dissolvuntur. At juxta sententiam nostram est altius conscendendum, et licet humano arbitrio nequitiam et perditionem incredulorum tribuamus, tamen credentium fidem, perseverantiam, ipsamque ad vitam aeternam destinationem a speciali Dei beneplacito, atque speciali operatione eidem beneplacito respondente, petendam arbitramur. Neque hic necesse erit curiose disputare, utrum Deus vitam aeternam prius decernat electis, dein gratiam efficacem, an e contra: sed id solummodo agendum est, ut probetur singularibus quibusdam personis Deo soli notis et gratiam efficacem et gloriam praedestinari, praeparari ac donari.
pass_a: From their position therefore, if it be asked, Why did these believe, those not believe? Why did these persevere, those not persevere? Why were these predestinated to eternal life, those not? all these questions are dissolved by the willing and not-willing of human choice. But according to our position one must ascend higher, and although we attribute the wickedness and perdition of unbelievers to human choice, yet we judge that the faith of believers, perseverance, and the very destination to eternal life are to be sought from the special good pleasure of God, and from a special operation answering to the same good pleasure. Nor will it be necessary here to dispute curiously whether God first decrees eternal life to the elect, then efficacious grace, or the contrary: but this alone is to be done, that it be proved that to certain singular persons known to God alone both efficacious grace and glory are predestinated, prepared, and gifted.
pass_b: On their view, ask why these believed and those did not, why these persevered and those did not, why these were predestinated to eternal life and those not — every question dissolves by human choice's willing and not-willing. On ours one must ascend higher: though we attribute unbelievers' wickedness and perdition to human choice, yet believers' faith, perseverance, and destination to eternal life are to be sought from God's special good pleasure and a special operation answering it. No need to dispute curiously whether God first decrees eternal life to the elect then efficacious grace, or the reverse — only to prove that to certain singular persons known to God alone both efficacious grace and glory are predestinated, prepared, and gifted.

title: Cap. VI thesis vs Remonstrants; Faustus Semipelagian axioms exploded
latin: Dicunt etenim et defendunt Remonstrantes, decretum praedestinationis sive electionis non cadere in quenquam, quem Deus non praevidit et consideravit ut credentem et ad extremum usque vitae habitum in fide perseverantem. Nos autem dicimus, praedestinationem antecedere hanc praevisionem; ita ut illi soli a Deo praevideantur et considerentur tanquam perseveranter credentes, quos Deus antecedente electionis suae proposito decrevit tales facere, factosque ad vitam aeternam perducere. Explodimus igitur illa Fausti Semipelagiani axiomata, quae non multum abludunt a mente et sententia Remonstrantium: qualia sunt; Salus hominum non in praedestinatione Factoris, sed in operatione famulantis collocata est. Non fuit specialis aliqua Dei munificentia erga credentes. Praedestinatis non est aliquorum bonorum causa. Praedestinatio ad justitiam pertinet. Nisi praescientia exploraverit, praedestinatio nihil decernit. Hisce omnibus opponimus hanc sententiam nostram; Praedestinationem singularium personarum ad vitam ex mero Dei beneplacito oriri, et non ex praevisis ullis humanae voluntatis operationibus: quin-etiam omnium bonarum operationum quae ad vitam aeternam ducunt, gratiam electionis causam antecedaneam ac fontem esse, non praemium aut mercedem sequentem. Argumentis jam agamus, ac ostendamus, merum Dei beneplacitum, non praevisam fidem ex una parte, et infidelitatem ex altera, facere primam discriminationem electorum et praeteritorum.
pass_a: For the Remonstrants say and defend that the decree of predestination or election does not fall upon anyone whom God has not foreseen and considered as believing and persevering in faith even to the last habit of life. But we say that predestination precedes this foresight; so that those alone are foreseen and considered by God as perseveringly believing, whom God by the antecedent purpose of his election has decreed to make such, and having made them to lead through to eternal life. We therefore explode those axioms of Faustus the Semipelagian, which do not much differ from the mind and position of the Remonstrants: such as; The salvation of men is placed not in the predestination of the Maker, but in the operation of the servant. There was not some special munificence of God toward believers. Predestination is not the cause of certain goods. Predestination pertains to justice. Unless foreknowledge has explored, predestination decrees nothing. To all these we oppose this our position; That the predestination of singular persons to life arises from the mere good pleasure of God, and not from any foresight operations of the human will: nay even that of all good operations which lead to eternal life, the grace of election is the antecedent cause and fountain, not a following reward or wage. Let us now deal with arguments, and show that the mere good pleasure of God, not foresight faith on one side and unbelief on the other, makes the first discrimination of the elect and the passed-by.
pass_b: Remonstrants say and defend that the predestination or election decree falls on no one God has not foreseen and considered as believing and persevering in faith to life's last habit. We say predestination precedes that foresight — so only those are foreseen and considered by God as perseveringly believing whom God by the antecedent purpose of his election decreed to make such and, having made them, to lead to eternal life. We therefore explode Faustus the Semipelagian's axioms, not far from Remonstrant mind: Salvation of men is placed not in the Maker's predestination but in the servant's operation. There was no special divine munificence toward believers. Predestination is not cause of certain goods. Predestination pertains to justice. Unless foreknowledge has explored, predestination decrees nothing. Against all these we set ours: predestination of singular persons to life arises from God's mere good pleasure, not from any foresight operations of the human will — nay, of all good operations leading to eternal life, election's grace is the antecedent cause and fountain, not a following reward or wage. Now to arguments: mere divine good pleasure, not foresight faith on one side and unbelief on the other, makes the first discrimination of elect and passed-by.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 1: Augustine — praedestinatio is foresight and preparation of God's benefits
latin: Primum argumentum petetur a definitionibus Praedestinationis variis, definiente Augustino; Praedestinatio est praescientia et praeparatio beneficiorum Dei, quibus certissime liberantur quicunque liberantur. Ubi observandum, Deum praescire ea beneficia sive gratiae dona, quibus adhibitis ipse liberabit singulares quasdam personas electas; dein, haec omnia illis praeparare, ac tandem, sicut praescivit et praeparavit, opportuno tempore conferre. Quid hic cogitari potest, quod non dimanet a mero Dei beneplacito, omnem humanae voluntatis actum praecedente? Praescivit enim Deus in electis illa dona gratiae quae ipse illis praedestinavit et praeparavit secundum gratuitam suam benevolentiam, quando illos elegit in Christo. Ut aperte etiam ex Apostolo colligitur Ephes. i. 3–4. &c. Si quis hic, ut purae Dei misericordiae tenebras offundat, praevisam fidem obtendat fuisse causam, aut conditionem antecedaneam, nugas egerit; cum fides sit unum ex praecipuis hisce beneficiis quae in praedestinationis decreto praeparantur hominibus electis.
pass_a: The first argument will be sought from the various definitions of Predestination, Augustine defining; Predestination is the foresight and preparation of the benefits of God, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Where it is to be observed that God foreknows those benefits or gifts of grace, by which applied he himself will liberate certain singular elect persons; then, prepares all these for them, and at length, as he foresaw and prepared, confers them at the opportune time. What can be thought here that does not flow from the mere good pleasure of God, preceding every act of the human will? For God foresaw in the elect those gifts of grace which he himself predestinated and prepared for them according to his free benevolence, when he elected them in Christ. As is also openly gathered from the Apostle Ephes. 1:3–4. &c. If anyone here, that he may pour darkness upon the pure mercy of God, put forward foresight faith as having been a cause, or antecedent condition, he will have dealt in trifles; since faith is one of the chief of these benefits which in the decree of predestination are prepared for elect men.
pass_b: First argument: from various definitions of Predestination. Augustine: Predestination is the foresight and preparation of God's benefits, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Observe: God foreknows those benefits or grace-gifts by which, applied, he will liberate certain singular elect persons; then prepares them all for them; and at length, as he foresaw and prepared, confers them at the right time. What here does not flow from God's mere good pleasure, preceding every act of the human will? He foresaw in the elect those grace-gifts he himself predestinated and prepared by free benevolence when he elected them in Christ — as Eph. 1:3–4 also openly shows. To cast darkness on pure divine mercy by putting foresight faith as cause or antecedent condition is trifling — faith is one of the chief benefits prepared for the elect in the predestination decree.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 1: Aquinas, Vasquez — preparation of grace cannot depend on foresight faith
latin: Sed missa Augustini definitione, audiamus ipsos Scholasticos. Aquinas dicit, Praedestinationem nil aliud esse quam praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro. Hominem autem in massa corrupta, perdito, ne suspicari quidem possumus ei hanc gratiam et gloriam praeparari ex antecedente aliqua fidei perseverantis in eodem homine consideratione. Ridiculum est enim dicere, Deum homini decernere et praeparare illam gratiam, quam prius ut habitam et obtentam consideravit. Idem Aquinas alibi; Praedestinatio est quaedam ratio ordinis aliquorum in salutem aeternam in mente Divina existens. Atque mox subjungit, Exsecutionem hujus ordinis esse passive in praedestinatis, active autem in Deo. Si praedestinatio sit ordinatio quorundam in salutem, non debemus cogitare homines quosdam per fidem perseverantem prius ordinatos ad vitam, imo in ipso quasi vitae vestibulo positos, priusquam a Deo eligantur, aut praedestinentur. Sed ipsos Jesuitas defensionis nostrae hostes acerrimos audiamus. Sic igitur Vasquez, Praedestinatio est propositum aeternum Dei, quo gratiam alicui praeparat in vitam aeternam. Propositum praeparans gratiam quae ducit ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter, non potest ex praevisa hominum fide dependere, cum haec fides sit illa ipsa gratia de qua loquimur: Ad meram ergo Dei voluntatem referatur est necesse. Haec tam clara veritas extorsit Jesuitae ingenuam hanc confessionem, Discretio praedestinatorum a reprobis incipit ante consensum ipsorum absolute praevisum. ergo ante praevisam fidem, aut merita qualiacunque, quae sine consensu voluntatis humanae ne intelligi quidem possunt.
pass_a: But Augustine's definition being passed by, let us hear the Scholastics themselves. Aquinas says that Predestination is nothing other than the preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future. But a man in the corrupt mass, lost, we cannot even suspect that this grace and glory are prepared for him from some antecedent consideration of persevering faith in the same man. For it is ridiculous to say that God decrees and prepares for a man that grace which he first considered as had and obtained. The same Aquinas elsewhere; Predestination is a certain reason of the order of some unto eternal salvation existing in the Divine mind. And presently he subjoins, That the execution of this order is passively in the predestinated, but actively in God. If predestination is an ordination of certain ones unto salvation, we ought not to think certain men by persevering faith first ordained to life, nay placed as it were in the very vestibule of life, before they are elected or predestinated by God. But let us hear the Jesuits themselves, the fiercest enemies of our defense. Thus therefore Vasquez, Predestination is the eternal purpose of God, by which he prepares grace for someone unto eternal life. A purpose preparing grace which leads infallibly to eternal life cannot depend on foresight faith of men, since this faith is that very grace of which we speak: It is necessary therefore that it be referred to the mere will of God. This so clear truth extorted from the Jesuit this ingenuous confession, The discrimination of the predestinated from the reprobate begins before their consent absolutely foreseen. therefore before foresight faith, or merits of whatever kind, which without the consent of the human will cannot even be understood.
pass_b: Passing Augustine's definition, hear the Scholastics. Aquinas: Predestination is nothing but preparation of grace now and glory hereafter. A man in the corrupt lost mass — we cannot even suspect that grace and glory are prepared for him from antecedent consideration of persevering faith in him. It is ridiculous to say God decrees and prepares for a man the grace he first considered as already had and obtained. Elsewhere Aquinas: Predestination is a certain reason of ordering some to eternal salvation existing in the divine mind — and the execution of that order is passively in the predestinated, actively in God. If predestination is an ordination of certain ones to salvation, we must not think some men by persevering faith first ordained to life — nay placed as it were in life's vestibule — before God elects or predestinates them. Hear even the Jesuits, fiercest enemies of our defense. Vasquez: Predestination is God's eternal purpose by which he prepares grace for someone unto eternal life. A purpose preparing grace that leads infallibly to eternal life cannot depend on foresight faith — that faith is the very grace in view — so it must be referred to God's mere will. That clear truth extorted this candid Jesuit confession: discrimination of predestinated from reprobate begins before their consent absolutely foreseen — therefore before foresight faith or any merits, which without human-will consent cannot even be understood.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 1 close: Arminius's own definition — first ratio from theologians' consensus
latin: Postremo audiatur ipse Arminius; Praedestinatio, inquit, est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo, quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, vita aeterna donare. Hic in praedestinatione duplex decretum involvitur: unum, Volo cunctis fidelibus dare vitam: alterum, Volo hisce certis personis dare fidem. Utrumque ex Dei gratuita et pura misericordia, neutrum ex praevisa fide aut aliqua humana operatione, dependet. Frustra igitur fidei praevisae conditionem praemittunt praedestinationi, quam omnes Theologi in ipsa praedestinationis definitione agnoscunt esse gratuitam, et fidei omnisque gratiae salutiferae scaturiginem. Atque haec sit prima nostra ratio, petita a communi consensu Theologorum in definienda ipsa Praedestinatione.
pass_a: Finally let Arminius himself be heard; Predestination, he says, is the decree of the good pleasure of God in Christ, by which he has from eternity determined with himself to gift with eternal life the faithful whom he has decreed to gift with faith. Here in predestination a double decree is involved: one, I will to give life to all the faithful: the other, I will to give faith to these certain persons. Both depend on the free and pure mercy of God, neither on foresight faith or any human operation. In vain therefore do they put a condition of foresight faith before predestination, which all Theologians in the very definition of predestination acknowledge to be free, and the spring of faith and of every saving grace. And let this be our first reason, sought from the common consent of Theologians in defining Predestination itself.
pass_b: Finally hear Arminius himself: Predestination is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. Predestination involves a double decree: I will give life to all the faithful; and I will give faith to these certain persons. Both depend on God's free pure mercy — neither on foresight faith or any human operation. Vainly then they put a foresight-faith condition before predestination, which all theologians in defining predestination itself acknowledge as free, and the spring of faith and every saving grace. Let this be our first reason — from the common consent of theologians in defining Predestination itself.

lemmas.gloss: give life to faithful / give faith to certain persons
